svg.title: Proposed Syn record lifecycle and acknowledgement states
svg.desc: A local signed save creates local durability. Authorised peer exchange creates replication evidence. Submission does not establish acceptance. Community ordering and deterministic validation produce finalised accepted or rejected outcomes. A local query view reports its checkpoint and projection lag. External anchoring is optional.
svg.text: A save, a receipt and finality are different facts
Proposed Syn lifecycle · illustrative states, not a running demonstration
1. Sign and save locally
Canonical bytes, signature and durable outbox
local_durable
2. Exchange with authorised peers
Verify records and retain peer acknowledgements
replicated · still provisional
3. Submit a bounded admission batch
Current authority, exact bytes and dependencies
submitted · outcome pending
During a quorum outage
Local authoring can continue; finality waits.
A two-by-two split cannot commit with four validators.
4. Finalise and validate deterministically
Retain backend evidence and exact outcome.
finalized_accepted / finalized_rejected
5. Build the accepted query view
Expose checkpoint, proof scope and projection lag.
projected
Optional external checkpoint anchor
Commitment only; separate access and cost decision
anchored_external
What finality does establish
An accepted record under a named community policy.
It cannot certify truth, understanding or external action.
States are separately retained evidence: replication counts, finality proofs and projection positions remain inspectable.
No screenshot or benchmark is implied. A real implementation demonstration belongs to a later phase.
